AGENDA
  GLENDALE CITY COUNCIL
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the City webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, Amazon Fire, iOS and
Android devices using a free app called Cablecast and choosing "Glendale TV" from the menu.
Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas.
Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the
meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that
agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for
assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are
received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review
in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting or as soon as
practicable. Please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City
provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak
in their native language.
  JUNE 24, 2025

ROLL CALL

  a. Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation: Topadzhikyan v. City of
  Glendale, L.A.S.C. Case No. 22SSTCV36445
  b.

   Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation: Janfaza v. City of Glendale,

  c. Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation: Significant exposure to
  litigation pursuant to subdivisions (d)(2) and (e)(2) of Government Code Section
  54956.9
  d. Public Employee Appointment – Director of Finance
  e. Public Employee Appointment – General Manager, Glendale Water & Power
  f. Public Employee Appointment – Fire Chief
  g. Conference with Labor Negotiators. The City-designated negotiator attending the
  closed session is: Mayor Ara Najarian. The unrepresented employee position is:
  City Manager

2.  REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA – 6:00 PM
  Roll Call
  a. Flag Salute: Council Member
  b. Invocation: Chaplain Donte Carty, Glendale Police Department
  c. Report of the City Clerk, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the June 24, 2025
  Regular Meeting of the Glendale City Council was Posted on June 20, 2025, on the
  Bulletin Board Outside City Hall.

3.  PRESENTATIONS AND APPOINTMENTS
  a. Agenda Preview for the Meetings of Tuesday, July 1, 2025
  b. Professional Development Center Check Presentation to City of Glendale for
  Workforce Training Grant
  c. Proclamation Declaring June 12, 2025, National Control Room Workers’
  Day Honoring Water and Power Employees

4.  CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are Routine and May be Acted Upon by One Motion. Any Member of Council or
  the Audience Requesting Separate Consideration May do so by Making Such Request
  Before Motion is Proposed.
  a. City Clerk, re: Award of Contract for FY 2025-2026 Legal Advertising for the City of
  Glendale
  1. Motion Awarding a Contract to HLR Media, LLC DBA Glendale Independent, sole
  responsible bidder, Specification No. 4018
  b. Glendale Water and Power, re: Award of a Professional Services Agreement (PSA) to
  Harper & Associates Engineering, Inc. for Water Storage Facility Rehabilitation
  Projects
  1. Motion authorizing the City Manager, or his designee, to execute a three-year
  Professional Services Agreement (PSA) with Harper & Associates Engineering, Inc.,
  to act on behalf of the City as Owner’s Engineers specializing in the design and
  oversight of City water storage facility rehabilitation projects for a total not-to-exceed
  amount of $450,000
  c. Public Works, re:
  Award Construction Contract for the Babe Herman Restroom Renovation Project
  TYPED 6/20/2025 12:46:45 PM
  06 24 25
  2  CC
   1. Motion authorizing the City Manager or his designee to execute a construction
  contract with Williamson Construction Co. Inc., for the Babe Herman Restroom
  Renovation Project, Specification No. 3978, in the amount of $275,000, plus a 10%
  contingency of $27,500, for a total amount not to exceed $302,500
  d. Public Works, re: Amendments to Multiple PSAs for Additional Design, Engineering,
  and Construction Management Services for San Fernando Road Beautification
  Phase II Project, and On-Call Engineering Services for Public Works Project
  1. Motion authorizing the City Manager or a designee to execute a contract amendment
  to Contract No. 8001984 with Mark Thomas & Company, Inc., to increase the contract
  amount by $59,660 to perform additional landscaping and irrigation design for the San
  Fernando Road Beautification Phase II Project
  2. Motion authorizing the City Manager or a designee to execute contract amendments
  to the following PSAs to provide additional engineering services in support of various
  PWD projects:
  a. Contract No. 8002222 with Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc., to increase the
  on-call traffic engineering services contract amount by an additional $200,000
  b. Contract No. 8002237 with KOA Corporation, to increase the on-call traffic
  engineering services contract amount by an additional $200,000
  c. Contract No. 8002258 with Twining, Inc., to increase the on-call geotechnical,
  soils engineering, and material testing services contract amount by an additional
  $150,000
  d. Contract No. 8002407 with Mark Thomas & Company, Inc., to increase the
  on-call construction management and inspection services contract amount by
  $750,000
  e. Contract No. 8002238 with NV5, Inc., to increase the on-call construction
  management and inspection services contract amount by $200,000
  3. Resolution of appropriation to appropriate additional funds for the Metro’s NoHo to
  Pasadena Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Project

  e. Community Services and Parks, re: Verdugo Workforce Development Board’s
  Submission Request for Approval of Local Workforce Development Plan 2025-2028
  1. Motion to approve the Verdugo Workforce Development Board’s Local Workforce
  Development Plan 2025-2028; approve submission of the Verdugo Workforce
  Development Board’s Local Workforce Development Plan 2025-2028 to the California
  Workforce Development Board and the State of California Employment Development
  Department; and authorize the Mayor and City Manager or designee to execute all
  relevant documents with the State of California, and the United States Department of
  Labor for the plan’s approval, implementation, and use
  f. Community Services and Parks, re: Elderly Nutrition Program Subaward of Grant
  Funds from County of Los Angeles Aging and Disabilities Department for FY 2025-
  2026 baseline funding and Modernizing Older Californians Act (MOCA) funding
  allocation of $490,900
  1. Motion to accept $443,300 in Elderly Nutrition Program (ENP) baseline funding and
  $47,600 in MOCA funding from Los Angeles County Aging and Disabilities (AD) for FY
  2025-2026; and authorize the City Manager or a designee to execute Subaward
  ENP252604 period July 2025 – June 2026 to accept and implement funding

5.  CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS

  TYPED 6/20/2025 12:46:45 PM
  06 24 25
  3  CC
 6.  COMMUNITY EVENT ANNOUNCEMENTS (3-Minutes; 5-Speaker Limit)
  Per Mayor Policy, This Item Also Permits Speakers Wishing to Speak Under General Oral
  Communications, Subject to the Three Minute Time Limit. Discussion is Limited to Matters Not
  on the Agenda.

7.  ADOPTION OF ORDINANCES

8.  ACTION ITEMS
  a. Glendale Water and Power, re: Solar Energy Power Sales Agreement: 30-Year Power
  Sales Agreement (PSA) with Southern California Public Power Authority (SCPPA) for
  Purchase of 25 MW from Milford Solar II Project
  1. Resolution authorizing a 30-year Power Sales Agreement (PSA) with Southern
  California Public Power Authority (SCPPA) for the purchase of 25 MW (or equivalently,
  an 8.3% entitlement share of the 300 MW contract capacity) of renewable solar
  energy and environmental attributes from the Milford Solar II Project, and finding that
  the project is exempt from the requirements of the Californi
  b. City Clerk, re: Consideration of Support of State Bills Recommended by the
  Commission on the Status of Women
  1. Motion providing direction on bills as recommended by the Commission on the Status
  of Women
  c. Finance, re: Adoption of the City’s FY 2025-26 Gann Appropriations Limit
  1. Resolution Adopting FY 2025-26 Gann Appropriations Limit
  d. Finance, re: FY 2024-25 Glendale Water and Power Transfer
  1. Resolution Reducing the Percentage of Operating Revenues to be Transferred from
  Glendale Water and Power (Electric) to the General Reserve Fund for Fiscal Year
  2024-25

9.  HEARINGS
  a. Finance, re: FY 2025-26 Citywide Budget Hearing and Adoption
  1. Hold a Public Hearing on the FY 2025-26 Proposed Citywide Budget and Changes to
  the Citywide Fee Schedule
  2. Resolution Adopting the FY 2025-26 City of Glendale Budget
  3. Resolution Modifying Existing Fees for Parking Services Provided by the City and
  Adopting Changes to the Comprehensive Citywide Fee Schedule for FY 2025-26
  4. Motion to Increase the Citywide Authorized Salaried Position Count
  5. Resolution Providing for the Establishment of Classification Titles and Compensation
  for Employees of the City of Glendale Covered by the Glendale Management
  Association Memorandum of Understanding, including Employee Relations Exempt
  Classifications
  6. Resolution Providing for the Establishment of Classification Titles and Compensation
  for Employees of the City of Glendale Represented by the International Brotherhood
  of Electrical Workers, Local 18
  7. Resolution Providing for the Establishment of Classification Titles and Compensation
  for Employees of the City of Glendale Covered by the Glendale City Employees’
  Association Memorandum of Understanding, including Confidential and Hourly
  Classifications
  8. Resolution Adopting the Glendale Water & Power Public Benefit Programs Plan and
  the Low Carbon Fuel Standard Programs Plan for Fiscal Years 2025-26 and 2026-27

  9. Resolution of Appropriation for FY 2024-25 to Transfer Funds from the Parking Fund
